label: system
description: Data related to a system that is not authorization or operations data.
examples:
Data we generate on our end, such as: 
document_id, channel, app_name, app_version, app_display_version, distribution ID, submission date/timestamp (i.e. time we received the ping on our edge servers), experiment_id, experiment_branch, enrollment_id, glean_client_annotation_experimentation_id, etc, window_start, window_end

label: system.authorization
description: Data used to manage access to the system.

label: system.operations
description: Data used to operate the systems.
examples: ETL monitoring data, backend systems telemetry with no user IDs, sample IDs

label: user
description: Data related to a user that cannot be categorized with one of the sub-categories, includes events coming out of User Activity

label: user.account
description: Data related to a user's account that cannot be categorized with one of the sub-categories, includes creation and registration information

label: user.account.fxid

label: user.account.contact

label: user.authorization
description: What a user is authorized to do, including the permissions and type of access granted

label: user.behavior
description: Data related to a user's behavior or actions, that is not considered browsing, search or purchase history
examples:
button click counts, interaction data (how often do you use x feature), activity_segment
impression/exposure data fits here - as a user had to do something to be in a place to see the impression.

label: user.behavior.attribution
description: User's attribution data (information about how a user first came to use a product)

label: user.behavior.browsing
description: User identifiable browsing data

label: user.behavior.browsing.categories
description: User's non-specific browsing history (general categories and top level domains, no specific URLs)

label: user.behavior.browsing_history
description: User's browsing history (specific urls)
examples:
https://www.bestbuy.com/site/pioneer-55-class-led-4k-uhd-smart-xumo-tv/
UTM parameter get both user.behaviour.browsing.urls and user.behavior, as it could be specific place or did a specific thing to get in the attribution or campaign

label: user.behavior.media_consumption
description: User's content consumption, click and scroll data
examples: time on page, clicks, interactions, ex: viewing videos, articles read, URI count, ad clicks, ad impressions, # of unique URLs visited, sponsored tiles clicks, impressions

label: user.behavior.purchase_history
description: User's purchase (subscription) or donation history

label: user.behavior.search
description: Data related to a user's search behavior
examples: SAP, unknown, organic, tagged_sap, # of searches done

label: user.behavior.search.provider
description: Search provider information

label: user.behavior.search.topic
description: User's non-specific search history (general categories, keywords). No specific search terms

label: user.behavior.search.term
description: User's specific search history
examples: "LED TVs", "bullseye rash on leg", "are grapes safe for dogs"

examples: Cookie settings, opt-ins and outs, Enhanced Tracking Protection settings, location and camera permissions

label: user.settings.installs
description: User's add-ons and installations

label: user.telemetry
description: Data we calculate based on other information such as device and interaction data.
examples:
Fields calculated based on usage data - for example, DAU, WAU, MAU (# of daily active users, # of weekly active users, # of monthly active users, # of new profiles)

Also includes fields based on a client's usage history - for example, days_active_bits, days_seen_bits, days_seen_bytes, days_since_active, first_run_date, first_seen_date, is_new_profile, active_hours, active_hours_sum

Also being used to record fields that track how well processes are running in the browser

Also includes fields like - session_count

Also used to count how often certain processes are used - how often are different parts of devtools being used (i.e.  JS debugger, JS profiler, inspector, etc)

How often different web page (CSS) elements are being used (so we know which ones to prioritize for improvements, debugging, etc)

gfx_compositor (type of graphics compositor being used), max # of tabs open at one time
